text: How do noise cancelling headphones work? It's very physics-y. So it's very engineering-y. There are microphones on the outside or inside of the headphones. Some headphones are called feedforward. They have the microphone on the outside and they pick up the noise before it reaches your ear. Some headphones are called feedback, they pick up the noise after it reached the ear, closer to the speaker. And then the digital signal processor analyzes the waveform and reconstructs it in real time. It gets the frequency, amplitude, phase. And then it creates the anti-noise. The exact same sound, but inverted, opposite phase. So when the noise meets the anti-noise, it will cancel out, because the peaks will meet the troughs and cancel out. And that's very good for low frequency, constant noise, like airplane engine noise, air conditioning noise, road noise. And not so good for higher frequency, more transient noises. Like a baby crying or a door slamming. Those are more difficult to cancel. And also, you still have some passive noise isolation from the ear pads themselves. And they cancel a bit more higher frequency noise. And then you have hybrid noise cancellation that combines both. So it's just picking up noise, inverting it, adding it back to cancel out. And you will get more quieter sound, but it's not absolute silence.
